vision: Make injury.bot an AFP-friendly pilot where people can shape their own application through an agent. Preserve the maintained base application while supporting isolated personal variations, approved extensions and upstream updates. Develop AFP as a separate platform and compatibility standard, using injury.bot and law.bot as pilots without derailing their primary products.
principles: Start with a plain-language request. Let the coordinator explore the desired outcome, propose an approach and explain tradeoffs.
Keep a user's customization isolated from other users and firms. Never copy private evidence, sessions or credentials into a fork.
Protect authentication, tenant boundaries, evidence provenance and independent attorney review decisions.
Support a path to separate databases and higher-compute runtimes for demanding customizations. These are planned capabilities, not installed services.
Consider developer revenue through explicit compute upgrades and reusable, shareable features. Show cost and obtain authorization before provisioning paid resources.
Track local bug fixes and a path to reporting them upstream, testing updates, resolving conflicts and rolling back.
An MCP interface is one integration surface. Fork isolation, deployment, versioning, data ownership and update reconciliation still need implementation.

checkpoints.title: Configurable agents and settings
checkpoints.detail: Existing firm/platform instructions, memory, model routing, installed skills and encrypted credentials support configuration. They do not provide arbitrary code customization.

checkpoints.title: Text and voice actions
checkpoints.detail: The coordinator executes registered server tools with permission checks and action receipts. AFP discussions can use this interface; no coding or deployment tool is installed.

checkpoints.title: Separate anatomical engine
checkpoints.detail: Human Atlas is independently maintained and pinned into the host build. This is a useful versioned component boundary, not a user-fork runtime.

checkpoints.title: Verified releases and cost visibility
checkpoints.detail: AWS deployment verifies release state. AI usage and pricing settings expose supported server usage estimates. Per-user deployment, arbitrary compute upgrades and live voice token metering are not implemented.

checkpoints.title: AFP memory and discussion
checkpoints.detail: Super-admin AFP Management maintains direction, progress and recommendations. Text and voice tools read current memory and save notes. This tracks AFP development; it does not certify AFP compatibility.

gaps: Define and validate an AFP manifest with supported extension points and protected boundaries.
Build an isolated customization runtime and data ownership contract, including optional separate databases and graphics compute.
Add a coding agent with reproducible bug reports, tests, preview, authorized activation and rollback.
Implement upstream update reconciliation and conflict review without losing personal customizations.
Define feature sharing, developer approval, compute pricing, portability and a compatibility validator or registry.
